Container.aiRules: Reach for this named layout intent before Box/sx. maxWidth MUST use the semantic width scale ('content' | 'max'), never a raw px value. Do NOT use the deprecated `padding` prop — it is a no-op; apply padding via Surface or a Stack instead. Usage (default responsive 12-col): <Grid> <Grid.Item colSpan={6}>…</Grid.Item> <Grid.Item colSpan={6}>…</Grid.Item> </Grid> Usage (responsive auto-fit): <Grid layout="auto-fit"> <Card /> <Card /> </Grid>

SegmentedControl.description: SegmentedControl " segmented selection input for compact mutually-exclusive choices. The active×hover×pressed×disabled×secondary state matrix is expressed through `cva` compound variants keyed by `active` / `interaction` (the live-or-frozen-demo hover/pressed/rest sub-state) / `variant` / `disabled`, each resolving to the same `--semantic-*` custom properties the pre-Tailwind inline styles referenced — same tokens, same pixels, just Tailwind classes instead of a `style` object. Per ADR-015 this control keeps its own hover/focus tracking (per-segment `string | null` cardinality) rather than the shared `useInteractionState` single-element machine; only the class composition changed, not the state machine feeding it.

Tag.description: Tag — interactive filter and category chip. The outer <button> carries the accessible 44px hit target directly via the size token while the inner pill keeps the visible surface compact. Colors (background, border-color, color) live in the pill's cva variants, painted through `group-hover`/`group-active` so the pill reacts to interaction on the shared outer button (converted off the former .hds-tag-btn/.hds-tag-pill theme.css rules for #60 — same behavior, now token-driven Tailwind classes). The `active` prop (aria-pressed selected state) is not one of the variant contract's four axes — it's expressed as the pill's `selected` cva variant, carrying the same rest → hover → pressed → focus-visible state matrix the contract expects, just keyed by selection instead of tone/size/density.

a11yRules.rule: When used as interactive chip (onClick), must have role="button" and keyboard activation

Page.description: Page — standard page shell. Wraps page content in Container (width constraint) and applies the canonical vertical padding so content breathes against the viewport edges on scroll. Use as the outermost element of any new page so vertical rhythm is consistent across the system without per-page reinvention. Page intentionally does not render its own footer — the shell is the single source of truth. Use Container directly only for full-bleed surfaces (sketches, hero sections, embedded canvases) where the page owns its own vertical padding. TabsContent.description: Tabs — Radix-backed underline tabs (Root, List, Trigger, Content). Underline pattern math: - TabsList carries `border-b border-border/40` (the divider, half-strength so it anchors the strip without competing with content). - TabsTrigger has `border-b-2 border-transparent -mb-px` at rest. The `-mb-px` offsets the trigger DOWN by 1px so the trigger sits on top of the list divider; the active 2px bottom border visually REPLACES that 1px segment instead of stacking on it. - Active state pairs the underline with a soft `bg-accent/5` tint that extends down into TabsContent — the active tab visually "claims" its content panel (folder-tab affordance, modern-soft). Overflow: TabsList is horizontally scrollable (`overflow-x-auto whitespace-nowrap`) for cases like /ops/atlas with 8 tabs at narrow viewports. Scrollbar chrome is hidden cross-browser (-webkit / firefox / IE).

Box.description: Box — polymorphic layout primitive with a token-first `sx` engine. `sx` is a deliberate SUBSET of MUI's sx — not all of CSS-in-JS is a feature: - Spacing shorthands (m/p/gap family) take the t-shirt scale ('xs'|'sm'|'md'|'lg'|'xl' → `--semantic-space-scale-*`, hds#206) through the resolver Stack's `gap` shares. Numbers still resolve as a count of 4px units (`p: 4` is 16px), and the deprecated 'tight'|'normal'|'inset'|'spacious' still read `--semantic-space-layout-*`, fixed px that compact density does not remap. HDS source may not use raw integers (check-spacing-vocabulary). - `color`/`bgcolor`/`borderColor`/`fill`/`stroke` resolve dotted token keys ('content.primary', 'surface.raised', 'border.subtle', 'accent', 'accent.hover', 'feedback.success', …) to the matching semantic CSS var. - Responsive `{ xs, sm, md, lg, xl }` objects compile to `min-width` media queries off the HDS breakpoint scale. - `&`-prefixed keys ('&:hover', '& > *', '&[data-state=open]') nest a selector, composable with responsive values. - Everything else passes through as a plain camelCase→kebab-case CSS declaration (numbers get `px` unless in the unitless allowlist). See `box-sx.ts` for the pure resolver + hashing/injection engine.

Box.aiRules: Reach for Stack/Grid/Container/the every-layout primitives first. Use Box `sx` ONLY for genuinely one-off layout. sx colors/spacing MUST use token keys, not raw hex/px. Prefer named layout primitives over ad-hoc flex.

Sidebar.description: Sidebar — fixed-width rail beside fluid content, no media query. Every Layout reference: https://every-layout.dev/layouts/sidebar/
Sidebar.aiRules: Reach for this named layout intent before Box/sx. Sidebar expects EXACTLY two children — the rail and the content — passed in that order. `side` controls which one visually renders as the rail; DOM order is unchanged. gap MUST use a semantic space step, never raw px. sideWidth and contentMin are CSS length dimensions (not spacing) — a length string like '16rem' or '50%' is expected, matching the check-hardcoded-spacing gate's own dimension-prop exemption. Do NOT use Sidebar for more than two regions — use Grid.

Switcher.description: Switcher — flips a row to a column below a width threshold, no media query. Every Layout reference: https://every-layout.dev/layouts/the-switcher/
Switcher.aiRules: Reach for this named layout intent before Box/sx. gap MUST use a semantic space step, never raw px. threshold is a CSS length dimension (not spacing), e.g. '30rem'. `limit` unconditionally forces the stacked (column) layout once there are more than `limit` children, regardless of container width — use it to stop a row from thinning out into an unreadable N-up strip. Do NOT use Switcher for content that should always wrap in place — use Stack with `direction="row"` and `wrap="wrap"`.

Pin.description: Pin — sticky-pin an element within its scroll region.
Pin.aiRules: `top` is a CSS length offset (a dimension, not a spacing step). Give the pinned element a TALLER scrolling parent so it has room to travel. For the scroll-scrubbed animation inside a pinned scene, use CSS `animation-timeline` (see Reveal) or `useScrollProgress` from `@hirobius/design-system/scroll`. See ADR-021.

Reveal.description: Reveal — reveal-on-scroll primitive via CSS scroll-driven animation.
Reveal.aiRules: Content is fully visible by DEFAULT; the effect applies only where `animation-timeline` is supported AND the user has not requested reduced motion (both fall back to visible, never stuck hidden). Pick `animation` from the fixed set — do not hand-roll keyframes. For momentum/inertia scrolling wrap the app in `SmoothScroll`; for a scroll-progress value in JS use `useScrollProgress` — both from `@hirobius/design-system/scroll`. See ADR-021.

usage.whenNot: A single line of text, or choosing from a list.

CardBody.description: Card — surface container with slot anatomy (12d-card-anatomy). Slot anatomy (DESIGN.md §"Card Anatomy"). Status, progress, and metadata are layout-bearing — they live in slots, never inline next to prose. <Card variant="accent"> <Card.Header metadata={<Badge tone="warning">in-progress</Badge>}> <Card.Title>Discovery phase</Card.Title> <Card.Description>Stakeholder interviews and audit prep.</Card.Description> </Card.Header> <Card.Progress value={42} max={100} label="5 / 12 tasks" /> <Card.Metric label="Retainer" value="$3,500" sub="Active" /> <Card.Body>…</Card.Body> <Card.Footer>…</Card.Footer> </Card> Slot reservations: - Header: title (h3) + optional description (caption) + optional metadata zone (right-aligned, holds <Badge> / <Tag> for status, never raw spans). - Progress: full-width 4px bar in a reserved 16px vertical rail. Owns its spacing — never crowds adjacent prose. - Metric: single label-uppercase + big value (h2) + optional sub-line. Reserved vertical block. Use multiple side-by-side via flex/grid container. - Body: prose, lists, structured content. NO inline status, progress, or thin colored bars. Group sections via separate <Card.Body> blocks. - Footer: actions, secondary metadata, timestamps. `variant`: 'default' (borderless) | 'accent' (2px accent border) — the structural axis, for highlighted entries like "recommended package". `tone`: neutral | danger | success | warning | info — the fixed feedback axis (#60 variant contract), for status-driven cards where the border IS the signal. `variant`/`tone` together replace hand-rolled `pkgHighlight`-style overrides. Legacy props (padding / gap / noPadding / as / style) are retained. Existing callers that pass raw children continue to work; new callers should prefer compound parts + `padding="none"`. Depth comes from semantic.color.border.default (role.border) at rest; elevation tokens are not bound by default — pass `className="shadow-..."` for a hover/floating treatment on interactive cards.

DialogClose.description: Dialog — modal dialog (shadcn baseline, compound parts). shadcn-baseline implementation (8s-7): Radix Dialog primitive (@radix-ui/react-dialog) themed with role tokens. Provides focus trap, scroll lock, ESC-to-close, backdrop scrim, and portal mounting out of the box. <Dialog> <Dialog.Trigger asChild> <Button>Open</Button> </Dialog.Trigger> <Dialog.Content> <Dialog.Header> <Dialog.Title>Confirm</Dialog.Title> <Dialog.Description>Are you sure?</Dialog.Description> </Dialog.Header> <Dialog.Footer> <Dialog.Close asChild> <Button variant="secondary">Cancel</Button> </Dialog.Close> </Dialog.Footer> </Dialog.Content> </Dialog> Surface uses role.popover (semantic.color.surface.overlay) + shadow-overlay (semantic.shadow.overlay from 8e-1). The scrim is role.scrim (semantic.color.surface.scrim) at 60% alpha: dark in both themes, black in dark mode. The overlay portals into the nearest `data-hds` scope so it inherits the active theme; pass `container` to override. The close affordance is rendered as an absolutely-positioned X inside Content; pass `hideClose` to opt out for fully-custom layouts.

Tooltip.description: Tooltip root. Bakes in the Radix Provider so a single `<Tooltip>` is self-contained — no app-level provider required. Controlled via `open`/`onOpenChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultOpen`.

usage.when: Name an icon-only control, or add a short hint that appears on hover and keyboard focus.
usage.whenNot: Anything interactive, text people need to finish a task, or a hint touch users must see (touch has no hover).

useInstead.reason: interactive or longer content that opens on click
a hint that must stay visible

keyboard.effect: Opens the tooltip when the trigger receives keyboard focus.
Closes the tooltip and keeps focus on the trigger.
Moves on to the next control and closes the tooltip.

Menu.description: Menu root + parts. Controlled via `open`/`onOpenChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultOpen`.

slots.name: trigger
slots.description: The element that opens the menu (Menu.Trigger).

usage.when: Offer a list of actions from a trigger, closed until opened.
usage.whenNot: Choosing one value for a form field, or a set of options that must stay visible.

useInstead.reason: choosing a value for a form field

keyboard.effect: Opens the menu from the trigger and highlights the first item.
Moves the highlight; it stops at the first and last item.
Jumps to the first or last item.
Highlights the next item that starts with the typed letter.
Selects the highlighted item and closes the menu.
Closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger.
Does not leave the open menu.

Popover.description: Popover root + parts. Controlled via `open`/`onOpenChange`, or uncontrolled with `defaultOpen`.

usage.when: Anchor interactive content, such as a short form, a filter set or a picker, to a trigger people click to open.
usage.whenNot: A short label on hover or focus, a list of actions, or a decision that must block the page.

useInstead.reason: a short label shown on hover or focus
a list of actions
a decision that blocks the page

keyboard.effect: Opens the popover from the trigger and moves focus inside it.
Closes the popover and returns focus to the trigger.
Cycles focus inside the open popover; the page behind stays reachable.

usage.when: Let people tick one or more independent options, or a parent choice that is partly selected.
usage.whenNot: An immediate on/off setting, or a choice of exactly one option from a set.

useInstead.reason: a setting that applies as soon as it flips
exactly one choice from a set

FormActions.description: Form footer with one fixed order: destructive (far left, if any), then secondary, then primary last and right-most. Gap is the tight layout token.

MetricTile.description: One metric tile: eyebrow label, `heading2` value, caption sub line, on a raised surface at one fixed min-height. Wraps `Card.Metric` (the sibling with the eyebrow / h2 / caption scale) and adds the surface and the fixed height, so a tile needs no enclosing `Card`.

MetricTiles.description: A row of `MetricTile`s. The grid has `min(tiles, 4)` columns, so three tiles fill three columns and never leave an empty fourth. The default for any row of headline numbers on a screen; use `Stat` only for an inline number inside prose or a dense list, `Card.Metric` only inside an existing `Card`, and `StatusTile` for state with notes (never a number).

PageHeader.description: Screen header: breadcrumb slot, the title at the one canonical page-title size (`heading2`), a status slot and an actions slot. Every screen has exactly one. `display` and `h1` type are reserved for marketing and landing surfaces.

DataTableSection.description: Section heading and toolbar over a `Table`. Row actions are consumer nodes in a trailing column, the table scrolls horizontally on narrow widths without a `minWidth` from the caller, and zero rows shows an `EmptyState`.

DestructiveSection.description: Titled danger zone: a title, an explanation, and one danger `Button` that opens an `AlertDialog`. Pressing the button never runs the action; only the dialog's confirm does. Place it last on the screen, below the form.

HdsFrame.description: Layout primitive — vertical or horizontal flex container on the 8px grid. Padding and gap from {0,8,16,24,32,48,64}; surfaces use semantic.color.surface.* tokens, never raw hex. Structural frames are rectilinear (no border-radius); only Card-wrapping frames pick up semantic.radius.card.

HdsHeading.description: Semantic heading wrapper. Maps level={1,2,3} to a typography token AND the matching h-tag (h1/h2/h3). Never skip levels (h1 → h3 without h2). Headings are font-light (display, h1) or font-normal (h2, h3) — never bold. Use Text for non-heading display copy.

HdsLabel.description: Form-control label primitive. Uses semantic.typography.caption (uppercase, tracked, font-medium). Color is semantic.color.content.secondary by default; the required-asterisk takes semantic.color.feedback.danger. Always pairs htmlFor with the control id; never used for non-label microcopy.

HdsAvatar.description: User identity glyph. Square or circle, sized on the 8px grid (24/32/40/48/64). Initial-letter fallback uses semantic.typography.small (font-medium, never bold). Image variant is object-cover, never object-fill. Radius is semantic.radius.action for square or semantic.radius.pill for circle.
